column1: Tab 6c — Reflect and Meditate (Rituals / Prayer): the 7th and 8th support pathways (v3.2, October 2026)

Read this tab before building either module. It answers the founder's question (can these sit under an existing pathway?), defines both pathways in plain language, sets the gating and safety rules the engine must apply, lists the tools, filters them by context, and points to the scenarios in Tab 0b that act as unit tests. The eight support pathways are now: Regulate, Express, Execute, Dump, Adapt, Reflect, Connect and Meditate (Rituals / Prayer). None of them is ever shown to the user as an 'intervention'; the user sees one plain-language card.

column2: Both start with getting thoughts out.
column4: Dump promises no structure and nothing to do. Reflect adds questions and a takeaway. Folding them would break Dump's promise to people who are overloaded.
column7: Keep separate. Dump can hand off to Reflect later, never the other way round in distress.

column4: Express shapes words for someone else (a message, a draft). Reflect is for the user's own understanding. Reflect often feeds Express (self-advocacy), which is a hand-off, not a merge.
column7: Keep separate, with a Reflect -> Express hand-off (pattern 35).

column2: Both can follow a hard moment.
column4: Regulate changes how you feel NOW. Reflect looks BACK and needs a calmer state; doing it under distress risks rumination.
column7: Keep separate; Reflect is gated by RF-1 and RF-2.

column2: Real overlap for breath-led and grounding tools.
column4: Regulate tools are short (about 1-3 min), body-first and can be used anywhere. Meditation, ritual and prayer are intentional practices tied to meaning, identity or faith, often longer and scheduled.
column7: Split by a clear boundary: Breathe and Ground micro-tools STAY in Regulate; longer practice, rituals and prayer live in Meditate.

column4: Adapt changes the conditions (pace, setting, order). A personal ritual is the user's own practice.
column7: Adapt can CALL a saved ritual from Meditate during a transition; the ritual itself lives in Meditate.

column4: Connect is about people. Prayer is the user's practice, alone or with others.
column7: Meditate holds the practice; Connect offers the faith or community group if the user wants people.

column1: Recommendation: keep both as stand-alone pathways (7th and 8th). If the team ever had to merge, the least-bad fits would be Reflect -> Express and Meditate -> Regulate, but both merges would lose safety gating (rumination and meditation contraindications) and faith neutrality, and would stop the team measuring whether each one actually helps. The user-facing label is 'Meditate'; inside it the user chooses Meditate, Rituals or Prayer.
